reason: E1 and E3 support that Cr substitution and lower temperature promote phase separation, and E3 shows that 600°C alone on AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi gives multi-scale (not uniformly refined) separation; no evidence supports that a two-step anneal (1000°C then 600°C) yields refined nanoscale precipitates, nor that such refinement increases coercivity via domain wall pinning. E2 notes the coercivity mechanism is not well understood, and the cited evidence partially contradicts the predicted refined microstructure from the proposed two-step treatment.
premises: Cr substitution for Co promotes phase separation into B2+BCC in AlCoFeNi
Two-step annealing (1000°C then 600°C) refines B2+BCC phase separation to nanometer scale
Nanoscale B2+BCC microstructure increases coercivity via domain wall pinning
Cr substitution reduces saturation magnetization due to antiferromagnetic nature
Single-step 1000°C anneal of AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi gives coarse, not refined, phase separation
